target: QEMU AArch64 virt machine with PCI VirtIO sound and WAV audio backend
command: QEMU_VIRT='-machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -m 1024 -device ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=/tmp/zeal-short-tone-bridge-regression.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' python3 scripts/check-compat.py --probe-source-fast --probe-source tests/compat/VirtioSoundProbe.ZC --probe-source-call VirtioSoundProbe
checks: Guest UART reported virtio-snd PCM playback ready (S16 48 kHz stereo).
On this rebuilt ISO, the source probe called Sound(60), waited 250 ms, stopped the tone, and returned 0x2a.

The QEMU WAV backend captured 12,348 stereo frames at 44.1 kHz (about 0.28 s); left and right channels matched, peak amplitude was 7,000, and sign transitions measured about 441 Hz after backend resampling.
scope_note: This verifies the QEMU VirtIO sound transport, stream setup, tone sample generation, and WAV-backend capture. It does not verify audible output in live UTM or on Raspberry Pi hardware, nor runtime behavior of every sound-dependent application. The QEMU WAV header retains streaming zero-length fields, so the PCM payload was inspected directly.
